children: has cleared a key U.S. antitrust hurdle for its planned acquisitions of Boeing's Wisk Aero, SkyGrid and Insitu businesses, removing one source of uncertainty around a transaction that could materially broaden Archer's reach beyond electric air taxis into autonomous aviation and defense technology. The deal still needs additional regulatory approvals, but Archer expects the acquisitions to close by the end of 2026.

Archer is best known for developing electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft, or eVTOLs, aimed at short-distance urban transportation. The Boeing transactions would expand that strategy by adding autonomous aircraft, airspace-management software and defense capabilities.

Archer said the waiting period required under the Hart-Scott-Rodino Antitrust Improvements Act expired at 11:59 p.m. EDT on September 18. That satisfies one of the conditions required to complete the acquisitions.
The expiration does not mean the deal is fully cleared. Remaining regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions still need to be satisfied before Archer can take control of the Boeing assets.
Still, the antitrust milestone reduces one of the more visible execution risks surrounding the transaction.

The strategic implications are significant. Wisk gives Archer exposure to autonomous electric aircraft development, while SkyGrid brings airspace-management technology. Insitu adds unmanned aircraft systems and defense capabilities, potentially giving Archer a broader commercial and government opportunity set.
ACHR shares were down about 1.4% in premarket trading despite the regulatory progress, suggesting investors are still weighing the cost, integration complexity and timing of the acquisitions.
For Archer investors, the next catalyst is straightforward: whether the Boeing transactions actually close by year-end.

Watch remaining regulatory approvals, financing terms and management's integration plans. The biggest upside would come from Archer showing that Wisk, SkyGrid and Insitu accelerate revenue opportunities rather than simply expanding its cost base.
The key risk is execution. Archer is already trying to commercialize eVTOL aircraft, so absorbing three additional aerospace businesses could stretch capital and management resources.
Clearing HSR reduces regulatory uncertainty, but investors still need evidence that the enlarged portfolio can improve Archer's path toward sustainable commercial scale.

title: Archer Aviation Sends Strong Signal With Boeing Move
